facts.content: Patient reports shortness of breath and a weird sensation in the lips and tongue after a bee or wasp sting.
facts.source_text: CC: Dyspnea + lip/tongue “weird” sensation after bee/wasp sting

facts.content: Patient was stung on the right arm a few minutes ago.
facts.source_text: Sting to R arm “few min ago”

facts.content: The sting site has a mild erythematous rash and a puncture mark with no marked swelling.
facts.source_text: → mild erythematous rash, puncture mark, no marked swelling

facts.content: The patient experienced brief shortness of breath earlier, which is now mild and stable.
facts.source_text: Brief dyspnea earlier; currently mild, stable

facts.content: The patient is anxious about progression of symptoms.
facts.source_text: anxious re progression

facts.content: Patient has a history of eczema.
facts.source_text: PMH: eczema

facts.content: Patient has episodic anxiety and is not on medication for it.
facts.source_text: PMH: eczema; episodic anxiety (no meds)

facts.content: Patient is allergic to penicillin, which causes a rash.
facts.source_text: Allergies: penicillin (rash)

facts.content: Patient works as a computer scientist and lives alone.
facts.source_text: SH: Computer scientist, lives alone

facts.content: Patient owns a cat and has no known pet or food allergies.
facts.source_text: owns cat, no known pet/food allergies

facts.content: Patient is conversing in full sentences and appears in no distress.
facts.source_text: General: Conversing in full sentences, no distress

facts.content: Lips, oral mucosa, and oropharynx appear visually normal with no stridor.
facts.source_text: Airway: Lips, oral mucosa, oropharynx visually normal; no stridor

facts.content: Breathing appears unlabored on video examination.
facts.source_text: Resp: Breathing unlabored on video

facts.content: There is a small puncture site on the right arm with mild redness and a blotchy rash, without surrounding swelling or warmth.
facts.source_text: Skin: Small puncture site R arm with mild redness, blotchy rash; no surrounding swelling/warmth

facts.content: Localized allergic reaction to insect sting with no current systemic involvement.
facts.source_text: 1. Localized allergic reaction to insect sting, currently no systemic involvement

facts.content: Anxiety secondary to the insect sting event.
facts.source_text: 2. Anxiety secondary to above event

facts.content: Recommended over-the-counter chlorphenamine 4 mg tablet, one tablet every 4 to 6 hours as needed, or a daily non-sedating antihistamine alternative.
facts.source_text: Antihistamine: OTC chlorphenamine 4 mg tab; 1 tab q4-6 h PRN or daily non-sedating alternative

facts.content: Patient was educated about signs of anaphylaxis including lip or tongue swelling, stridor, and respiratory distress and advised to call 999 or attend the emergency department if these develop.
facts.source_text: Educate: signs of anaphylaxis (lip/tongue swelling, stridor, resp distress) → call 999/ED if develop

facts.content: Advised to monitor the arm for spreading erythema, heat, or pus and to seek care if these develop due to concern for possible cellulitis and need for antibiotics.
facts.source_text: Wound care: monitor arm for spreading erythema, heat, pus; seek care if develops (possible cellulitis → abx)

facts.content: Patient was provided written information on anaphylaxis and reassured about the low risk of a delayed reaction.
facts.source_text: Provided written info on anaphylaxis; reassurance re low risk of delayed reaction

facts.content: Patient was advised to re-contact their GP or Babylon service or attend accident and emergency if symptoms worsen or new concerns arise.
facts.source_text: F/U: Re-contact GP/Babylon or attend AE if symptoms worsen or new concerns
